label: Experimental Lake Simcoe — unvalidated depth-averaged wind response
componentOrientation: true east / true north in local equirectangular approximation

wind.name: ECCC National Climate Archive — Barrie-Oro hourly observations

rawUnits.WIND_DIRECTION: tens of degrees true, meteorological direction from

assumptions: Land-station wind applied uniformly to the lake; no over-water speed correction.
Nominal 10m wind height is assumed from the ECCC standard; a station-specific anemometer-height record was not verified.
Hourly observations are short-period observation averages, not hourly-mean winds; the samples are linearly interpolated in time.
UTC_DATE is used directly as UTC. LOCAL_DATE is EST throughout the source record, with no daylight-saving adjustment.
Wind forcing is not a measurement of water current.

model.equations: Linearized rotating shallow-water equations with variable undisturbed depth, nonlinear quadratic bottom drag, surface wind stress; no advective or thermal/density terms.
model.scheme: Arakawa C-grid finite volume, depth-weighted skew-symmetric corner Coriolis, SSP-RK3
model.initialCondition: Rest with eta0=0 at2026-10-01T05:00:00Z;259.0-hour wind-forced spinup before mean window.
model.boundary: No-normal-flow on all land/island faces and closed Atherley Narrows; no tributary/outlet forcing.
model.averaging: Trapezoidal time integral of east/north components, every solver step, over2026-10-12T00:00:00Z–2026-10-17T12:00:00Z; meanSpeed separately retained.

limitations: Experimental physics response, not observed/retrieved/validated currents.
Depth average cannot represent actual surface shear, thermal stratification, internal waves or baroclinic circulation.
Single land weather station applied uniformly, no over-water correction; nominal10m wind height assumed, not station-verified.
Closed narrows, no tributaries or outlet throughflow; avoid interpreting channel currents.
Historic interpolated bathymetry and 500m grid; unresolved small-scale coast and channels.
Constant uncertain bottom and air-water drag; numerical tests do not establish field accuracy.
The averaging window is the2026week, not a multiyear October climatology.
